title: Brute-force enumeration for two sum
summary: Represent all pairs of distinct array positions with an upper-triangular table.
context: The input consists of the integer array nums = [2, 7, 11, 15] (indexed from 0 to 3) and the target sum target = 13.

The problem asks for two distinct array positions whose elements sum to target and returns their indices (the element at a single position cannot be used twice). The brute-force approach runs two nested loops with outer index i and inner index j (j > i), checking each pair's sum in turn.
description: In the lower part of the figure, a four-by-four matrix lists 2, 7, 11, and 15 as both row and column headers and fills in only the six candidate sums in the upper-triangular region above the main diagonal—excluding both pairing an element with itself on the main diagonal and duplicate reversed pairs in the lower-left region. The table below takes its elements and candidate sums from the matrix; index pairs come from 0-based positions in the input, and pair expressions combine row and column headers.

At the intersection of row 0 (element 2) and column 2 (element 11), cell 13 is highlighted in violet-blue text. Following the code's left-to-right enumeration order, once the outer loop fixes i = 0 (element 2), the inner loop first computes 2 + 7 = 9 and immediately next computes 2 + 11 = 13, hitting the target and returning [0, 2] right away; the remaining candidate sums are drawn only to show the complete combination space, not because evaluation continues after a match.

frames.title: Brute-force enumeration for two sum
frames.explanation: The two nested loops take O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space, trading time for space.
